visible_text: Given BC = CD = DE = 16 cm and ∠BCD = ∠CDE = 90°, AB = AE and ∠BAE = 90°. Find the area of pentagon ABCDE. (A) 71 cm² (B) 128 cm² (C) 192 cm² (D) 224 cm²
reasoning: Since BCDE consists of three sides of a square with side 16 cm, its area is 16·16 = 256 cm². In triangle ABE, AB = AE and ∠BAE = 90°, so using the Pythagorean theorem with hypotenuse BE = 16 cm gives AB² + AE² = 256 ⇒ 2x² = 256 ⇒ x² = 128. The area of triangle ABE is ½·AB·AE = ½·128 = 64 cm². Therefore the area of pentagon ABCDE is 256 − 64 = 192 cm², which corresponds to option C.
